facts.text: Slipstream's defining feature is the price range. A liquidity provider chooses a lower and upper price bound where their capital operates. Narrow ranges concentrate capital and earn more per dollar but can fall out of range sooner; wide ranges earn less but stay active longer. A full-range Slipstream deposit behaves like a Basic Pool, and for that case, a Basic Pool is usually the more direct choice.
Under **Rewards**, select **AERO rewards** or **Fee rewards**. Each card shows its current APR. A greyed-out card means that reward type is not available for this pool.

The result is a flywheel: AERO Rewards attract liquidity. Liquidity enables trading. Trading generates revenue. Revenue rewards Token Operators. Token Operators direct allocation to productive pools. Emerging tokens bootstrap liquidity on-demand by attracting allocation. Protocols shape their trading environment. All participants are rewarded for contributing to efficient well-functioning markets.

This is a quickstart guide to everything you need to get started on Aero. In this guide you can see a breakdown of the core app functions: swapping a token, putting liquidity to work, staking AERO, and allocating AERO rewards. Each section covers one of Aero's core functions.
Emissions are the protocol's issuance of new AERO. That AERO is distributed as **AERO Rewards**: the reward stream that draws liquidity to the pools where trading happens.

Providing liquidity means depositing a pair of tokens into a pool so traders can trade against them. In return, the deposit earns a continuous stream of rewards on Aero. Liquidity is accessed through the Liquidity tab within the Aero app. **Liquidity** providers choose between two reward types: AERO Rewards (directed by Token Operators based on predicted volume) or a portion of trading fees. No single deposit can earn both.

Markets is the hub where sAERO holders (*Token Operators*) allocate, directing new emissions (*AERO Rewards*) to pools. In exchange, they receive Exchange Revenue streaming continuously from the pools where they have allocated.

Each allocation is a prediction of where liquidity is needed across the ecosystem, and together those predictions decide how AERO Rewards are split across pools. This is Predictive Allocation, and Markets is where it happens in the app.

Activation is a one-time event that confirms the pool's tokens meet the requirements for AERO Rewards. Once activated, a gauge directs AERO Rewards to the pool. The Governor contract can set a gauge cap to zero, which stops new AERO Rewards emissions.

A gauge cap is a ceiling on the AERO Rewards a single pool can emit. A Gauge Cap does not guarantee emissions by itself as emission distribution is still handled by Token Operators. Therefore gauges are not guaranteed to receive their cap.

Allocation Power is the measure of sAERO staking weight applied to a pool. The more Allocation Power directed to a pool, the higher that pool's AERO Rewards rate. A Token Operator's share of a pool's Exchange Revenue is calculated as their Allocation Power divided by the total Allocation Power allocated to that pool.
Allocation Power is the amount of AERO Rewards an sAERO stake can direct. It depends on how much AERO is staked and how much of the staking period remains.

Providing liquidity means depositing a pair of tokens into a pool so others can trade against them. In return you earn a share of the pool's activity. On Aero you choose whether a deposit earns trading fees (Fee-earning) or AERO Rewards (AERO-earning). See [Providing Liquidity](/products/liquidity).

In general, staking means committing a token for a period in exchange for rewards or rights in a protocol. On Aero specifically, staking is converting AERO into sAERO, which you then use to allocate AERO Rewards across pools and to earn Exchange Revenue. See [Staking](/products/staking).

AERO is the protocol's liquid native token, the asset traded, held, or received as AERO Rewards. sAERO is staked AERO that carries staking weight, earns Exchange Revenue, and is committed for the length of the stake. AERO holders can remain liquid; staking AERO into sAERO makes the staker a Token Operator, who allocates AERO Rewards across pools and earns Exchange Revenue. See [AERO and sAERO](/about/aero-and-saero).

Allocation Power is the amount of AERO staked multiplied by the staking duration remaining, calculated linearly. A larger stake or a longer remaining duration means more AERO Rewards the stake can direct. As the staking period runs down, Allocation Power decays linearly, unless the stake is set to Perpetual Stake, which holds it constant.

A Token Operator is an sAERO holder who directs Allocation Power to liquidity pools and keeps a share of the protocol's Exchange Revenue in return. The role sits at the center of Aero's flywheel: Token Operators stake AERO to receive sAERO, direct AERO Rewards to productive pools, those rewards attract liquidity providers, trading generates revenue, and that revenue flows back to the Token Operators who directed it.
Allocation Power is the amount of AERO Rewards an sAERO stake can direct to liquidity pools. It is also the measure that sets a stake's share of Exchange Revenue from each pool it allocates to.

Both pool types share the same gauge interface and cap logic. The difference is how rewards are distributed within that gauge based on each pool's structure. A Basic Pool distributes to every deposit equally by size. A Slipstream pool distributes only to deposits whose price range covers the current trading price. Slipstream pools use different tick spacings, which set how narrow a deposit's range can be. Only AERO-earning liquidity whose range covers the current price earns.

Each of the steps above represents one part of the AERO Flywheel. Traders pay fees on the pool. Those fees attract sAERO allocations and drive AERO Rewards to the pool. AERO Rewards attract liquidity providers to improve pool depth. Liquidity depth improves execution, better execution brings more trading, and more trading generates more fees.

* **AERO-earning.** The deposit receives an amount of AERO Rewards dependent in part on the size of the LP, the Allocation Power Token Operators have directed to that pool and on the pool's gauge cap. * **Fee-earning.** The deposit keeps a portion of the fees generated. No AERO Rewards accrue to it.

* **Slipstream pools** hold concentrated liquidity. The LP picks a price range, and the deposit is active and earning only while the pool's price sits inside it. Concentrating capital in a narrower band earns more per dollar while it is in range, and nothing when the price leaves. * **Basic Pools** hold full-range liquidity, so a deposit is always in range and never needs adjusting. Volatile pools suit pairs whose assets are not expected to track each other. Stable pools suit assets that trade near parity, such as two stablecoins.
Tick spacing sets range granularity: tighter for stable pairs, wider for volatile. When price leaves a range, the liquidity provider must widen, shift, or wait for it to return.

* **Pool Tape.** Records fee, volume, and volatility data per network at a governance-set cadence. Predictive Allocation, the dynamic fee module, gauge-cap automation, and external integrations read from it directly; no off-network infrastructure required. * **Exchange depth.** Slipstream pools are a core source of depth behind trading. Metaswaps can route cross-network trades into them, so an LP can earn from flow that originated on another network Aero operates on. * **AERO Rewards.** Set continuously by Token Operators who direct their Allocation Power to the pool.

* **Routes across Slipstream and Basic Pools.** A single quote covers both pool types (concentrated-liquidity and full-range) and any route hopping between them. Aero's routing engine automatically selects the best execution path across all available liquidity. * **Cross-network via Metaswaps.** When tokens sit on different networks, the Trade function runs a Metaswap, trading across networks in one flow with no separate bridge UI. Atomic settlement ensures the trade completes end-to-end. * **Dust auto-sweep.** Any tokens left over at the end of a multi-step flow return to the trader's wallet

* **There is no range to manage.** Basic Pools spread capital along the pool's whole price curve. * **Exiting an AERO Rewards deposit early can cost rewards.** Withdrawing within a short minimum holding period, set per pool, forfeits a share of the unclaimed AERO on the deposit. The forfeited AERO is not paid to the depositor. Adding to a Basic Pool deposit restarts the holding period, but rewards already claimed are kept. Fee-earning deposits have no early exit penalty. * **Leftover dust comes back automatically.** Adding liquidity rarely uses tokens in exactly the right ratio. Whatever is le
**Slipstream pools charge Dynamic Fees.** The fee rises when the pool price moves away from its recent time-weighted average price, up to a per-pool cap.

**Rebalancing**: Moving a concentrated-liquidity deposit from its current price range to a new one. Because a range is fixed once set, this closes the deposit and reopens it in the new range as a single transaction.

Most AMMs leak MEV to external searchers and sequencers. Slipstream instead captures MEV inside the pool, converting what would otherwise be lost to external actors into additional pool revenue. The mechanism differs by network. On select networks, a trade whose priority fee exceeds a threshold pays an extra fee that rises with the priority fee, up to a cap.

A Slipstream deposit is represented as an NFT, because each one has its own price range and its own accrued earnings. A Basic Pool deposit is represented by fungible LP tokens, since every deposit in the pool covers the same full range.

If the reward type and gauge are both as expected, the cause is usually range. A concentrated (Slipstream) deposit only earns while its range covers the current trading price. Outside that range it stops earning until price returns or the range is moved, and the AERO directed to the pool in the meantime goes to in-range deposits instead. It is never paid retroactively. A custom range can drift out and need adjusting by hand; a full-range deposit never goes out of range. None of this applies to Basic Pool deposits, which are always active across the full price curve. See [Slipstream](/features/

* **Token Operators direct AERO Rewards.** Allocation Power is the input to Predictive Allocation. Token Operators use their Allocation Power to direct AERO Rewards to pools. Those rewards flow to liquidity providers in the allocated pools, incentivizing them to supply liquidity where Token Operators predict volume will be highest. * **sAERO earns from every Aero revenue stream.** Exchange Revenue captured by protocol activity (trading fees, MEV capture, Liquidity Payments, Launch Payments, ancillary services) flows to Token Operators based on their Allocation Power. Each deposit earns one reward stream, chosen when the deposit is created. The app shows the two options as **AERO rewards** and **Fee rewards**, each with its current APR.

Under **Rewards**, select **AERO rewards** or **Fee rewards**. On a new pool, AERO Rewards do not flow until both tokens are listed and the gauge is active, so that card may be unavailable. A Fee-earning deposit keeps a portion of the fees generated from the first trade.

When a save moves Allocation Power from one network to another, a **Redirect allocation** window lists each network as **Successful** or **Pending** while the networks confirm separately. Pending is normal; wait until every network shows Successful. Moving Allocation Power off a network counts as a change to that network's allocation, so that network's cooldown applies.
A full-range Slipstream deposit (spanning the entire price curve) behaves identically to a Basic Pool because it earns from every price and requires no management.
AERO is Aero's native token. sAERO is the token created when AERO is staked. sAERO carries the right to direct AERO rewards and earn Exchange Revenue in return.

Other token models distribute passive yields. sAERO ties earnings to active participation: directing AERO Rewards to optimize liquidity flow. Token Operators use Predictive Allocation to determine where liquidity is needed, and direct new emissions toward those pools.
sAERO is the stake a holder receives when they stake AERO. It represents the right to allocate AERO Rewards to liquidity pools and to earn a share of the Exchange Revenue generated by those pools.
**AERO-earning liquidity**: A liquidity deposit set to earn AERO Rewards; its trading fees flow to Token Operators as Exchange Revenue. A deposit earns AERO Rewards or trading fees, never both.

**Aero Flywheel**: The self-reinforcing cycle at the center of Aero: allocations direct AERO Rewards, rewards attract liquidity, deeper liquidity attracts trading, and the resulting fees and Liquidity Payments draw further allocation.

**Predictive Allocation**: Aero's mechanism for continuous, concurrent, cross-network allocation of AERO Rewards and distribution of revenue. sAERO holders allocate at any time and earn based on the productivity of the pools they back. Replaces the weekly voting cycle.

Aero's MEV capture identifies MEV activity when the priority fee of the transaction doing a swap (the priority fee is what determines transaction ordering within a block) is above a defined threshold. The tax is then a fee charged (on top of the existing swap fee), which is a multiple of the priority fee value above the threshold. The tax works the same as other swap fees, directed to Token Operator rewards for staked LPs and as directly claimable rewards for unstaked LPs.

This is a unique role in the ecosystem. Token Operators decide which pools the protocol rewards, AERO Rewards draw liquidity to those pools, and deeper liquidity enhances trading. Because of that loop, Markets is central to the Aero token economy.

* **Pool volume.** Pools with higher trading volume generate more trade fees, increasing Exchange Revenue and APRs. When volume declines, APRs decline proportionally. * **Autopilot allocation.** Autopilot directs pooled Allocation Power to pools expected to generate the most revenue. If Autopilot reallocates to lower-volume pools, or if previously productive pools see reduced activity, APRs may decrease. * **Incentive programs.** Liquidity Payments and other incentives boost short-term APRs. When incentive programs end, APRs may decline. * **Network conditions.** MEV capture and other network-

Aero's MEV capture identifies MEV activity when the priority fee of the transaction doing a trade (the priority fee is what determines transaction ordering within a block) is above a defined threshold. The tax is then a fee charged (on top of the existing trade fee), which is a multiple of the priority fee value above the threshold.

A **gauge** is a contract that turns Token Operator allocations into AERO Rewards for a specific pool. Token Operators allocate a share of the constantly streaming AERO rewards through their selections. These rewards then stream to LPs that choose AERO-earning when depositing their liquidity.

The gauge serves as the collection point for all revenue flowing to the pool. Trade fees from the pool, Launch Payments, MEV capture, and Liquidity Payments directed to that pool all flow through the gauge. The gauge then routes this revenue to the appropriate recipients: AERO-earning deposits receive AERO tokens based on their share of active liquidity, and Token Operators receive the trading fees based on their proportional Allocation Power.
Cap status is visible in the Markets view, so Token Operators can see when a pool is at its ceiling and more Allocation Power would not increase its AERO Rewards.

A gauge is created automatically when a pool is created. The gauge starts in an inactive state. To activate a gauge and enable AERO Rewards for a pool, the pair must pass the gauge verification. Once listed, the gauge activates and begins distributing AERO Rewards based on Token Operator allocations.

The distinction lies in deployment timing. A newly created pool begins without allocation or AERO Rewards. Deploying a Launch Payment at registration triggers the pool's AERO Rewards from inception, enabling the pool to accumulate depth and support trading volume from day one. This contrasts with organic allocation growth, where a pool must establish market presence before attracting Token Operator interest.

This guide is for Token Operators who want to participate in the Aero ecosystem. AERO is staked to receive sAERO, which directs AERO Rewards to liquidity pools and earns a share of Exchange Revenue in return. The guide walks through the full flow: creating a stake, choosing how it is managed, allocating, and managing the stake afterward.

Staking AERO offers two direct benefits: the ability to direct AERO Rewards and the opportunity to earn Exchange Revenue. When sAERO is held, the Token Operator can allocate AERO Rewards to specific liquidity pools. This allocation directs where liquidity flows across the ecosystem. In return, the Token Operator receives Exchange Revenue: a proportional share of the trade fees and other revenue generated by the pools they allocate to. This creates a direct link between allocation decisions and earnings.
Predictive Allocation is Aero's mechanism for directing AERO Rewards and earning exchange revenue. It runs continuously on every network Aero supports and replaces the weekly voting cycle.

Predictive Allocation makes directing rewards continuous. Token Operators choose which markets the exchange should support with AERO Rewards, liquidity providers follow, and the Token Operators keep a proportional share of the revenue those markets produce. Backing a market early, and being right, likely earns the largest share of that revenue when it accrues. And because the prediction is an allocation, not just a bet, it helps bring about the outcome it predicts, moving liquidity ahead of demand.

When liquidity is provided to a Basic Pool, the capital is deployed along the pool's whole price curve automatically. There is no price range to set. The only choice is which reward stream the deposit earns. This guide starts from the pool list on the Liquidity page. Creating a new pool is covered in [Pool creation](/guides/pool-creation). Basic Pools come in two types:

* **Both tokens are deployed onchain** on the target network and their addresses can be verified. * **Both tokens are held in sufficient quantity** to seed the pool meaningfully. Thin initial liquidity leads to higher volatility and price impact. * **A fair price has been determined.** The app offers the current market price where it is available. * **The pool does not already exist.** If a pool for the same pair and type already exists, the app lists it and the flow becomes a deposit into that pool. * **The reward type choice is understood.** A new pool does not earn AERO Rewards until both t

* **The payment token is listed on the Token Registry.** Only listed tokens can be used to pay incentives. * **The pool is eligible.** A pool whose gauge is not active has no Token Operators earning AERO Rewards on it, so a stream there reaches nobody. The pool's overview page shows Not eligible on the Allocate card for pools that are not yet eligible. * **The wallet holds the full amount.** The whole amount transfers when the program is created. * **Token, amount, and dates are decided in advance.** There is no edit step after creation.

| Incentive type | Audience | When it's available | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Liquidity Payments** | Token Operators | After AERO Rewards activation | Growth tool: activates once AERO Rewards are live and governed by guidelines below |

AERO Rewards flow to pools continuously, determined by Token Operators directing emissions through Predictive Allocation. Pools with more allocated weight receive greater AERO Rewards. There is no weekly vote: allocation runs continuously and updates as Token Operators adjust. See [Predictive Allocation](/features/predictive-allocation).

Quotes update as the pool state changes, because other trades are executing against the same liquidity and dynamic fees respond to conditions. This is expected. The slippage tolerance is what protects against the price moving between the quote and execution.

MEV is value that bots extract from the ordering of transactions around a pool, and on most venues it leaves the system entirely. Aero captures a portion inside the AMM through a priority-fee tax on high-priority transactions, and that value accrues as pool fees. It arrives in the same fee flow as swap fees, so there is nothing separate to claim.

An AERO-earning deposit in a pool with no rewards flowing to it earns nothing, because its swap fees are routing to Token Operators while no AERO Rewards arrive in exchange. Switching the deposit to Fee-earning restores fee income, and the deposit can be moved elsewhere instead.

Two things. Direct influence over where AERO Rewards flow, by allocating to specific pools, and a claim on Exchange Revenue. Because revenue follows the pools a deposit allocates to, a staker's earnings track the productivity of the liquidity they direct.

Through Predictive Allocation. A Token Operator directs their stake's Allocation Power to one or more pools onchain, and AERO Rewards stream to those pools. There is no weekly cycle and no proposal to approve: allocation is a direct action taken by each holder. Each stake can be re-allocated once every 47 hours, the Allocation Cooldown.

Allocate, re-allocate, and claim. A Token Operator directs their stake's Allocation Power to pools, moves it when the pools they are backing change, and claims the Exchange Revenue that accrues. This is not optional upkeep: Exchange Revenue flows only to Token Operators actively allocating at the time it is generated, so a deposit that is never allocated directs no AERO Rewards and earns no Exchange Revenue.

sAERO is what AERO becomes when it is staked. It is an ERC-721, not a fungible token: each sAERO stake is an NFT with its own amount, stake period, and accrued revenue, and it holds the Allocation Power for that stake.

To the AERO-earning deposits in a pool, in proportion to each deposit's share of that pool's eligible liquidity. In a Slipstream pool only in-range liquidity is eligible, so a deposit sitting outside the range earns nothing while it is out.

For a Slipstream pool, pick a preset (**+/-3%**, **+/-8%**, **+/-15%**, or **Full**) or set the **Low** and **High** bounds directly. A narrower band concentrates the seed liquidity where price is most likely to trade; a wider band spreads it across a larger range.

On an AERO-earning deposit, 100% of the swap fees that deposit generates route to the Token Operators allocating to the pool, and the LP earns AERO Rewards in place of the swap fees. On a Fee-earning deposit in a Slipstream pool, the LP keeps a portion of the fees generated and the remainder goes to Token Operators.

They can also choose to earn a portion of the trading fees instead. Both paths incentivize strengthening of market depth where it's needed. 3. **Token Operators** stake AERO and direct rewards toward pools. Under **Price range**, pick a preset (**+/-3%**, **+/-8%**, **+/-15%**, or **Full**) or set the bounds directly. The **Low** and **High** cards each have minus and plus controls, with a **0** shortcut on Low and an infinity shortcut on High. The **Liquidity distribution** and **Historical price** charts (1D, 1W, 1M, 1Y) help place the range, and the pair toggle flips the price direction. Range bounds snap to the pool's price grid, so the exact low and high may adjust slightly to the nearest available prices.

It depends on the deposit. On an AERO-earning liquidity deposit, 100% of that specific deposit's swap fees route to the Token Operators who are actively allocating to the pool, and the LP earns AERO Rewards. A Fee-earning liquidity deposit keeps most (or all depending on the pool) of the fees it generates with a portion routed to Token Operators.

A staker is someone who stakes AERO and receives sAERO in return. Staking AERO grants Token Operator status, which is the protocol's term for the role, so the two words describe the same participant. A Token Operator allocates AERO Rewards to liquidity pools and earns Exchange Revenue from the pools they allocate to. Where a Token Operator allocates, 100% of the swap fees generated by the AERO-earning liquidity in that pool route to the Token Operators actively allocating to that pool, and the liquidity providers there earn AERO Rewards instead.

Exchange Revenue is all of the revenue the protocol captures and distributes to Token Operators: trading fees, MEV capture, Liquidity Payments, Launch Payments, and other ancillary protocol revenue. 100% of it flows to Token Operators based on the Allocation Power they direct to pools.

Routing is set per liquidity deposit, not per pool, and both kinds of deposit can sit in the same pool. An AERO-earning deposit sends 100% of the swap fees it generates to the Token Operators, and the liquidity provider earns AERO Rewards in return. A fee-earning liquidity deposit keeps a portion of the fees it generates and receives no AERO Rewards.

* **Impermanent loss,** covered above, which is the risk specific to providing liquidity. * **Price risk.** The deposited tokens stay exposed to their own price movement. * **Range risk.** A Slipstream deposit earns nothing while the price is outside its range. * **Smart contract risk.** Aero's contracts are audited, but no onchain protocol is risk-free. * **Changing rewards.** Token Operators can redirect Allocation Power away from a pool, which reduces or ends the AERO Rewards flowing to it.

The app labels each Slipstream pool with a CL number, such as CL 1 or CL 200. It is the spacing of the pool's price grid: lower numbers mean a finer grid and allow tighter price ranges. The CL number is set at pool creation and cannot be changed. One pair can have one pool per CL number.

A deposit's price range is fixed when it is created and cannot be edited. To move the range, withdraw the deposit and open a new one at the new range. Withdrawing is the point where any impermanent loss accrued so far is realized.

A volatility multiplier scales that base fee up in high-volatility regimes and relaxes it toward the base rate when the market is calm, so liquidity providers are better compensated for the arbitrage risk (LVR) that comes with enabling liquidity across different volatility regimes.

* **Ready.** The stake has an allocation waiting to be saved. * **Allocated.** The allocation is in place. The card shows **Cooldown time left**, or how long ago the allocation was saved. * **A percentage available.** Part of the stake's Allocation Power is not yet directed to any pool. * **Automated allocation.** The stake is on Autopilot and cannot be allocated manually.

The purpose is to compensate liquidity providers for the risk they carry during volatile stretches. For traders, it means fees are lower in calm markets than a single flat rate would be, and higher when volatility makes providing liquidity riskier.

A pool's tick spacing sets the minimum width for any range: CL1 allows ranges as narrow as 0.01%, while CL2000 requires ranges of roughly 20%. The range picker snaps to these predefined intervals rather than allowing arbitrary prices. Spacing is fixed when a pool is created and cannot change.
**Concentrated Liquidity (CL)**: Liquidity provided within a chosen price range rather than across the entire price curve. On Aero, concentrated liquidity is provided through Slipstream.

Slipstream is Aero's concentrated-liquidity AMM. Concentrated liquidity allows liquidity providers to specify a price range where their capital operates, rather than spreading it across the entire price curve. By concentrating capital into a narrower band, liquidity providers can earn more per dollar deployed on the price ranges where trading actually occurs.

Slipstream allows liquidity providers to concentrate capital within a specific price range, earning more per dollar than full-range Basic Pools. The trade-off: concentrated deposits require active management and carry greater impermanent loss if prices diverge sharply.

Placing liquidity within a chosen price range rather than spreading it across every possible price from zero upward. Because the capital is concentrated where trading actually happens, it is far more capital-efficient than full-range liquidity. The tradeoff is that it needs attention: a deposit stops earning when the price moves outside its range, and returns to earning if the price comes back.

Each Slipstream deposit is an ERC-721 token with its own ID, holding its range, liquidity and uncollected trading fees. Adding to an existing range uses the deposit-management tools rather than merging balances the way a fungible LP token would.

A swap fee, charged per trade and set by the pool. Slipstream pools use dynamic fees rather than one flat rate, so the fee responds to conditions instead of staying fixed. Basic Pools use a static fee set by the pool's fee module. Gas is also charged per trade by the network the trade occurs on. The quote shows the fee and gas before confirmation.

Rather than relying on historical data to decide where rewards go, Token Operators direct their Allocation Power to the pools where they believe liquidity is needed. Liquidity providers follow AERO Rewards to those pools, and the Token Operators allocated to a pool receive that pool's trading fees, MEV capture, and incentives (*exchange revenue*). The system gives individual Token Operators more agency to leverage their edge, and collectively improves the efficiency of the protocol.

Predictive Allocation is how sAERO holders direct rewards to LPs and earn Exchange Revenue. Instead of following a weekly epoch window, sAERO holders can select pools any time to direct AERO and receive a share of the Revenue generated by the pool. Pool revenue is distributed as it's earned.
Each trade takes a fee that accrues to Token Operators and liquidity providers. The fee rate is static, set by the pool's fee module, rather than the per-tick escalation used by Slipstream.

The AER Engine caps each pool's AERO Rewards as a multiple of its projected revenue, updated dynamically as conditions change (see [Gauge Caps](#how-it-works) below). Because the cap tracks revenue instead of a flat schedule, realized inflation moves with real activity rather than accruing on a set curve.

A token with thin liquidity incurs volatile price impacts, and that volatility can impact user decision-making. Liquidity Payments solve this by allowing projects to attract AERO Rewards rather than paying liquidity providers directly. This is more capital-efficient: a project's incentive budget goes further on Aero because the pool receives AERO emissions, compounding the impact of incentives. A fixed liquidity mining budget spreads thinly across many LPs; here, the same budget triggers additional AERO Rewards, making each dollar of incentives more powerful.

Payments are structured as continuous streams rather than one-time distributions. A Token Issuer funds a program by setting a token, a total amount, a start time, and a duration. Those tokens stream at a constant per-second rate to Token Operators (sAERO holders) who direct AERO to the pool. Only Token Operators who allocate receive the payments, creating direct alignment: allocators are rewarded, and their allocation brings AERO Rewards that attract and retain liquidity providers.

The first trade in each block computes the fee and every trade in that block pays the same rate, so a quote holds for the block. The volatility input is the pool's own price oracle. * **Basic Pools** spread liquidity across the entire price curve. Available in Volatile (uncorrelated pairs) or Stable (near-par assets) variants. No range management required. * **Slipstream** concentrates liquidity within a price range, offering more capital efficiency but requiring active management. For full mechanics, see [Slipstream](/features/slipstream) and [Basic Pools](/features/basic-pools).

A Slipstream pool divides the price curve into discrete levels called ticks. A deposit is defined by a lower and an upper tick and supplies liquidity to every tick between them. As trades move the price through ticks, the deposits whose range covers the current price are the ones filling those trades and accruing the pool's fees.

Within each tick range, Slipstream prices trades on the same constant-product curve as a Basic Pool: `x * y = L^2`, where L is the liquidity active in that range, computed on virtual reserves (the balances the range would hold if it spanned the whole curve). The more liquidity active at the current price, the less a given trade moves it, which is why a deep, well-placed range fills trades with less slippage than a larger thinly spread pool.

Aero coordinates how liquidity is distributed across markets. The revenue shared this way expands beyond trading fees to include MEV capture, Liquidity Payments, Launch Payments and other protocol income. Revenue flows to sAERO holders continuously as it accrues, creating faster feedback and more responsive capital redeployment than fixed-schedule distributions.
Aero runs on several networks, but AERO itself only exists on Base. On every other network, AERO rewards are paid in xAERO, a standard ERC-20 receipt token that stands in for AERO on that network.

AERO rewards are claimable on all networks. Liquidity providers may choose to claim AERO rewards on Base, or on the network where they are providing liquidity. Base is the network for the AERO token, xAERO is claimable on all other networks. Liquidity pools for AERO may not exist on every network, but all xAERO can be bridged back to Base for more efficient trading.

Issued AERO follows allocation to pools, and within a pool it reaches liquidity providers as AERO Rewards on their AERO-earning deposits. An LP who earns AERO can hold it, sell it, redeposit it as liquidity, or stake it into sAERO to become a Token Operator themselves. See [AERO and sAERO](/about/aero-and-saero).

**AERO Rewards.** Stream continuously, directed by Token Operator allocation to pools. The AER Engine (*Adaptive Emissions Rate*) governs the pace using two complementary controls: where rewards go (*allocation*) and how much value each pool receives (*gauge caps*).
**Gauge Caps.** Set a custom reward cap for every pool tied to its projected revenue: its swap fees, MEV capture, and Liquidity Payments combined.
**AER Engine**: One of Aero's two economic engines. It calibrates the rate at which AERO Rewards are issued to match market conditions, and reduces rewards to pools that are no longer productive.
**AERO Rewards**: Tokens that stream continuously to liquidity providers, flowing to each pool in proportion to the allocations Token Operators direct to it.
**Allocate / Allocating**: To direct AERO Rewards to specific pools as an sAERO holder. (Replaces "voting.")
**Allocation Power**: A Token Operator's capacity to direct AERO Rewards: the amount of AERO staked multiplied by the duration remaining. Perpetual Stake pins it at the maximum.

**Boosted Rewards**: A reward paid directly to liquidity providers in a pool, on top of the trading fees their deposit already earns. Anyone can fund them, including a network, an issuer, or a partner, and they are separate from AERO Rewards.

**Exchange Revenue**: The share of everything users pay across Aero that the protocol captures and returns to sAERO holders. It covers Pool Revenue (trading fees, MEV capture, Liquidity Payments, and Launch Payments), which goes in full to the Token Operators allocating to each pool, plus fees from Aero services beyond the exchange.

**Fee-earning liquidity**: A liquidity deposit set to keep a portion of the fees it generates; a dynamic protocol fee share still flows to Exchange Revenue. A deposit earns trading fees or AERO Rewards, never both.
**Gauge**: The per-pool contract that gathers a pool's allocations, AERO Rewards, trading fees, and Liquidity Payments. Only pools with an active gauge receive AERO Rewards.

**Liquidity Payments**: Tokens deposited to encourage sAERO holders to allocate AERO Rewards to a specific pool; they stream to the allocating Token Operators as Exchange Revenue. Also called incentives; the term for what was previously called bribes.
**MEV capture**: Aero keeping trading-related profit (MEV), such as from arbitrage, that outside bots would otherwise take, and returning it to liquidity providers and Token Operators.
**Token Operator**: An sAERO holder who actively allocates AERO Rewards to pools and earns Exchange Revenue in return. The primary term for this role; "sAERO holder" is the plain-language equivalent.
A deposit earns Trading Fees or AERO Rewards.
AERO Rewards reach each pool through Predictive Allocation. The more Allocation Power Token Operators direct to a pool, the higher its AERO Rewards rate, up to a dynamically updated cap per pool.

sAERO represents a staked AERO commitment. Token holders (*Operators*) use sAERO stakes to direct new protocol emissions (*AERO Rewards*). Token Operators direct AERO Rewards toward liquidity pools they choose. Those AERO Rewards incentivize liquidity providers, and that liquidity makes pools more efficient for traders. The liquidity funded by their rewards sends fees back to those sAERO holders.

AERO is staked for an amount and a duration from 6 months to 4 years. Alternatively, stakers can choose Perpetual Stake to maintain their stake at the 4-year maximum indefinitely. The sAERO balance and Allocation Power reflect the amount and the committed duration. Allocation Power is the power to direct AERO Rewards through Predictive Allocation, determining the holder's influence over protocol emissions.

Token Operators may only direct AERO Rewards to pools with an Active Gauge. New pools are created with a gauge, but the gauge must be activated before the pool is eligible to receive AERO Rewards and become available for Token Operator allocation.

* Direct the Operator's Allocation Power to pools across every network Aero is on. * Claim Exchange Revenue (*trading fees, MEV capture, Liquidity Payments, and Launch Payments*) as that revenue accrues. * Route the revenue, typically compounding back into sAERO.

* Trade fees from trading activity in allocated pools * MEV capture from activity in allocated pools * Liquidity Payments directed toward allocated pools * Launch Payments directed toward allocated pools

| Stage | Status | Behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | **Gauge Inactive** | Gauge exists but inactive | Pools are equipped with a Gauge but are inactive by default, pool trades and earns fees; no AERO Rewards possible | | **Gauge Activated** | One-time verification passed | Pool's tokens confirmed in listing; AERO Rewards begin flowing | | **Gauge Active** | Ongoing operation | Full reward distribution based on Allocation Power and cap |
`gauge cap = (projected time period fees (trading fees + mev tax revenue) + scheduled 48h incentives) x policy multiplier`

In practice this creates several scenarios for gauges. Most relevant, excess Allocation Power directed to a pool already at its cap does not add to its AERO Rewards (*unless a cap raise is justified based on accruing fees*). In this scenario, the Gauge Cap clips emissions at the current value of the projected fee-justified ceiling.

| Scenario | Outcome | | --- | --- | | **Pool below cap, Allocation Power increases** | Reward rate increases proportionally to new Allocation Power | | **Pool at cap, more Allocation Power allocated** | AERO Rewards are minted at the cap until the cap is updated | | **Pool receives Liquidity Payments** | Payments accrue through the gauge to Token Allocators | | **Gauge is inactive** | No AERO Rewards emit |

**Incentives** (*comprising Liquidity Payments and Launch Payments*) enable token issuers to bootstrap and deepen pool liquidity on Aero. A Token Issuer funds a program on a specific pool by setting a token, a total amount, a start time, and a duration. Those tokens stream at a constant per-second rate to Token Operators who direct AERO rewards to that pool, driving liquidity depth and supporting trading volume.

From the start time, the program streams at a constant rate of the amount divided by the duration, per second, until the end. Token Operators directing AERO Rewards to the pool accrue a share of everything streaming through it, proportional to their Allocation Power against the total weight allocated to that pool at each moment.

**Predictive Allocation** enables Token Operators to earn Exchange Revenue by directing their sAERO to pools expected to generate trading volume. As AERO Rewards stream continuously to those pools, Token Operators earn a pro rata share of the Exchange Revenue.

Exchange Revenue is what Token Operators earn for allocating. Each pool's revenue, which includes trade fees, MEV capture, and Liquidity Payments and Launch Payments from projects, flows to the Token Operators who allocate to that pool. A Token Operator's share of a pool's revenue is proportional to the Allocation Power directed to that pool relative to all other Token Operators allocating there.

Using Allocation Power from sAERO, Token Operators allocate AERO Rewards to pools. The allocation determines which pools receive AERO Rewards and which pools' revenue flows to the Token Operator. These steps apply to manual stakes. Autopilot stakes show **Automated allocation** on the **Allocate** tab and need no action here.

Select **+ Allocate** on a row to add that pool to a stake's allocation. The **Launching** tab lists pools about to launch or just launched. A pool earns AERO Rewards only once its gauge is active.

* **In range.** The current price is between the low and high bounds chosen for the deposit. The liquidity is actively enabling trades and earning rewards. * **Out of range.** The current price has moved outside the range. The liquidity is not being used and stops earning until price returns to the range. An out-of-range deposit also no longer holds both tokens: as price moves through the range, the liquidity is progressively traded into the token that is falling in relative value, and once price exits the range that conversion is complete. The deposit must be repositioned to resume earning.

A deposit earns only while the trading price is within the chosen range. Once price moves outside the range, earnings stop until price returns. Missed earnings are never paid retroactively: AERO directed to the pool while the deposit is out of range flows to in-range AERO-earning deposits instead, and if the pool has none it is not paid out to any deposit in that pool. Check the deposit's status under Portfolio > Deposits regularly.

Deposits earn rewards through one of two mechanisms. AERO-earning deposits receive a continuous stream of AERO Rewards directed to the pool by Token Operators. Fee-earning deposits keep a portion of the fees generated by the pool. Basic Pools offer straightforward liquidity provision with no active range management required.

* **AERO-earning deposits** receive AERO Rewards directed to the pool by Token Operators. Fees generated by AERO-earning liquidity route to the Token Operators who allocated to the pool. * **Fee-earning deposits** keep a portion of the fees generated by the pool. AERO Rewards do not accrue to Fee-earning deposits.

The pool trades and generates fees immediately. AERO Rewards depend on separate steps: both tokens must be listed, which is a governance action, the pool's gauge must be active, and the gauge's cap must be above zero. Until then the pool's overview page shows **Not eligible** on its **Allocate** and AERO APR cards. Registry review does not block the pool from trading.

A project deepening liquidity on an Aero pool pays for it with Incentives, also called Liquidity Payments: a token, an amount, and a start and end date, streamed to the Token Operators who allocate AERO Rewards to that pool. The stream runs at a constant rate, so Token Operators earn from the moment they allocate, and the creator can reclaim whatever streamed while nobody was allocating.

AERO Rewards are newly emitted AERO, released by the protocol. The emission rate is not flat: the AER Engine calibrates emissions to real activity, trimming rewards to pools that stop producing fees and holding each pool under a dynamically updated cap. Rewards concentrate where trading actually happens. See [Predictive Allocation](/features/predictive-allocation).

Liquidity provided in a pool and set to AERO-earning receives a stream of AERO Rewards directed to the pool by Token Operators. A pool qualifies to receive AERO Rewards once its gauge has been activated (which requires that both tokens are listed); the deposit screen shows the expected APR. Fee-earning deposits keep a portion of trading fees instead. See [Liquidity Management](/guides/liquidity-management).

Exchange Revenue is generated per-pool from that pool's trading activity: trading fees, MEV capture, Liquidity Payments, and Launch Payments. It flows only to Token Operators actively allocating Allocation Power to that pool, distributed continuously in proportion to each operator's allocation.

No. Aero does not pay AERO Rewards for executing swaps. AERO Rewards go to eligible liquidity deposits, and Exchange Revenue goes to Token Operators. A trader who wants to earn from the protocol can provide liquidity or stake AERO to become a Token Operator.

Indirectly. Token Operators direct AERO Rewards to pools, those rewards attract liquidity providers, and more liquidity in a pool means more depth. More depth means less price impact on the same trade size. Pools that receive sustained AERO Rewards tend to be the ones with the best execution.

No. Providing liquidity requires no AERO and no stake. Staking AERO to become a Token Operator is a separate role with separate earnings: Token Operators direct AERO Rewards to pools and earn Exchange Revenue. The two roles can be held at once, and many participants do hold both.

Acquire AERO and stake it. Staking converts liquid AERO into sAERO, an NFT that represents the stake and carries its allocation rights. The stake's Allocation Power is the amount of AERO staked multiplied by the staking duration remaining, so both size and duration determine how much AERO Rewards it can direct. Once the stake exists, its holder can allocate AERO Rewards to pools and claim the Exchange Revenue that accrues.
Which liquidity pools receive AERO Rewards, and in what proportion. That is the whole scope of the action. Allocation does not set fee structures, reward rates, or any other protocol parameter.
By the total Allocation Power directed at it relative to every other pool. Each pool's share of AERO Rewards is its share of allocations.

Yes. One sAERO stake participates across every network Aero operates on. The core token and allocation contracts live on a single home network, Base at launch, and each connected network runs a local deployment that receives its AERO Rewards rate from there and distributes it among its own gauges.

Yes. A Token Operator allocates to individual pools, and those pools sit on specific networks, so a single stake can direct AERO Rewards to pools on several networks at once. Predictive Allocation is concurrent and cross-network, so this does not require a separate stake or a separate action per network.

Yes. Staking AERO and providing liquidity are separate actions on separate stakes, and one user can hold both. A stake earns Exchange Revenue. A liquidity deposit earns either AERO Rewards or a portion of the trading fees it generates, depending on how the deposit is set up.

Allocation is proportional: a stake directs AERO Rewards in proportion to its share of the Allocation Power pointed at each pool, so a large stake carries proportionally large influence over the pools it backs. The AER Engine caps per-pool AERO Rewards based on anticipated productivity, so allocating heavily to a pool that generates little in fees does not translate into unlimited AERO Rewards for that pool.

The share of pool revenue that flows to the Token Operators who allocated Allocation Power to that pool. It comes from trade fees, MEV capture, Liquidity Payments and Launch Payments (incentives funded by projects), and other protocol fees.
